subject: religious-studies
title: The Golden Rule
welcome_lead: Discover the one simple rule that almost every religion in the world agrees.
meta_desc: KS3 Religious Studies adventure on the Golden Rule across world religions.
final_note: You can now explain the Golden Rule and where it appears in world religions.

concepts.def: Treat others as you'd like to be treated.
Give and take fairly with others.
Helping those in need with money or time.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Golden Rule says: 'Treat others as you would like to be treated.' Almost every religion teaches a version of this, including Christianity, Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, Buddhism and Sikhism.

Jesus said: 'Do to others what you would have them do to you.' Judaism's Rabbi Hillel said: 'What is hateful to you, do not do to others.' The Buddha said: 'Hurt not others with that which pains yourself.' Many cultures share this wisdom.
The Golden Rule applies in everyday situations: sharing with classmates, being honest with friends, not bullying, and helping others. It is a simple but powerful guide to behaviour.

Be the best at everything

mcqs.q: Which of these is closest to empathy?

mcqs.q: What is the problem of evil?
options: It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.

mcqs.q: What does the Buddhist doctrine of anatta teach?
options: Buddhists believe in a soul like the Christian or Hindu version.
Anatta means Buddhists have no personality.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
There is no permanent, unchanging self or soul — what we call 'self' is a constantly changing flow of five aggregates (skandhas). This is distinctively Buddhist and differs from the Hindu atman.

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
Christians believe in three different gods.
Anatta means Buddhists have no personality.
God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.
